assertions: uniswapV2Pair seeded with USDT/LAXO liquidity (LAXO addr > USDT addr enforced by BaseUSDTWA constructor)
balanceOf[DEAD] < MAX_SELL_BURN (1e26) so burn-from-pair branch executes
setup_calls: lp adds liquidity (lp excluded from fee)

post_vuln_state.custom_assertion: USDT.balanceOf(seller_after) > USDT.balanceOf(seller_before) + estimatedFairOutput AND pairLAXOReserveAfter ~= pairLAXOReserveBefore (net unchanged) AND pairUSDTReserveAfter < pairUSDTReserveBefore

attack_steps: seller approves router for LAXO; calls router.swapExactTokensForTokensSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens(amountIn, 0, [LAXO, USDT], seller, deadline)
Router transferFrom(seller, pair, amountIn) → triggers LAXOToken._transfer(seller, pair, amountIn)

Inside _transfer recipient==pair branch: 5% sellFee → contract; 95% burnAmount path takes super._transfer(pair, DEAD, burnAmount) burning LAXO FROM the pair, then pair.sync() commits reduced pair LAXO reserves, then super._transfer(seller, pair, burnAmount) refills pair LAXO back to original balance

Net effect on pair after _transfer: balance0(LAXO)=reserveLAXO_old (unchanged), but stored reserves report reserveLAXO_old - burnAmount; pair.balanceOf - reserve0 = burnAmount → router's _swapSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens path computes amountOutput = getAmountOut(burnAmount, reserveLAXO_old - burnAmount, reserveUSDT_old)
Pair.swap pays amountOutput USDT to seller; K-check passes since input is actually present in pair balance

After swap: pair LAXO balance=reserveLAXO_old (still unchanged), pair USDT = reserveUSDT_old - amountOutput. Loop drains pair USDT to ~0 while pair LAXO is preserved (each cycle limited only by 5% sellFee retention and MAX_SELL_BURN cap of 1e26)
preconditions: seller is not in _isExcludedFromFee
balanceOf[DEAD] < MAX_SELL_BURN before action
swap path uses router.swapExactTokensForTokensSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens (the standard for fee-on-transfer tokens)
MCGA sinks: LAXOToken._transfer (block_dep, lp_sync, custom_burn); KG seed: 2025-04 BTNFT_exp / general burn-from-pair-with-refill rugpull pattern

triage.drop_reason: Verification not run on BSC fork in this iteration (budget). Mechanism is structural and reproducible from static analysis: line 111 super._transfer(uniswapV2Pair, DEAD, actualBurn) and line 122 super._transfer(sender, recipient, burnAmount) bracket pair.sync() at line 112 — pair LAXO balance is restored AFTER reserves were reduced by sync(). Combined with router's fee-on-transfer swap path that recomputes amountOutput from post-sync reserves, every sell extracts USDT priced at artificially-low LAXO reserves while leaving pair LAXO inventory intact. K = reserveLAXO * reserveUSDT decreases monotonically per sell; bounded only by 5% sellFee and MAX_SELL_BURN (1e26). Any holder can drain pair USDT. Duplicate of existing holdout_laxo_full-1 (same case, same vector).

post_vuln_state.custom_assertion: After repeated 1-hour-spaced non-pair transfers, balanceOf[uniswapV2Pair] strictly decreases each tick (by 0.0208% of pair LAXO) while no offsetting refill occurs; pair LAXO drains toward 0 monotonically, and (reserveLAXO * reserveUSDT) strictly decreases (K-broken)

attack_steps: Wait 1 hour after startDeflation (or any prior deflation tick)
griefer.transfer(any_non_pair_addr, dust) — sender is not pair, conditions on L70-71 satisfied
Branch executes super._transfer(uniswapV2Pair, DEAD, balanceOf[pair]*208/1000000) — burns 208/1000000 = 0.0208% of pair LAXO with NO refill (unlike the sell path which refills)
pair.sync() commits the reduced LAXO reserves
Repeat each hour. Pair LAXO geometric decay r = (1 - 208/1000000) ≈ 0.999792 per tick; LAXO market price spikes; eventually pair functionally unusable while DEAD accrues toward MAX_BURN (1.869e26)
preconditions: owner has invoked startDeflation() (cannot be undone — lastDeflationTime is set once and cannot be reset)
Anyone with dust LAXO can call .transfer to keep the deflation timer ticking — no permissioned trigger
Combined with vuln #1 (sell-path USDT drain) gives full rugpull: USDT drained out, LAXO reserve auto-burned

triage.drop_reason: Verification not run on fork. Mechanism static-verified: branch L68-78 burns from pair WITHOUT refill (in contrast to sell branch L107-122 which refills) and is permissionlessly triggered by any LAXO transfer occurring ≥1 hour after the previous tick. Severity is medium — economic griefing rather than direct theft, but reduces liquidity provider exit value and inflates token price artificially. Rate-limited to once per hour so attack horizon is days/weeks not seconds, but no upper bound short of MAX_BURN.

assertions: Contract has accumulated USDT/other-token balance from sellFee → _swapTokenForFund → distributor → contract path, OR users have mistakenly sent tokens to LAXOToken
marketingAddress() returns the marketing wallet from IProject
setup_calls: Several sells have executed; some non-LAXO tokens held by LAXOToken

post_vuln_state.custom_assertion: marketing-controlled wallet may call emergencyWithdraw(USDT, marketing, contract.balanceOf(USDT)) and drain ALL non-LAXO ERC20 holdings of the contract to an arbitrary _to address — function only blocks _token == address(this) and _to == 0; no per-call cap, no timelock, no event flag distinguishing legitimate fee distribution

attack_steps: marketing wallet (or whoever controls IProject.marketingAddress()) calls LAXOToken.emergencyWithdraw(USDT_addr, attackerControlledAddress, type(uint256).max-ish) with _amount = contract USDT balance
L213 require passes (msg.sender==owner||msg.sender==marketingAddress() — marketing path);
L216 IERC20(_token).transfer(_to, _amount) sends USDT to arbitrary recipient
Same vector valid for any ERC20 the contract holds except LAXO itself
preconditions: marketingAddress is mutable post-deploy: anyone calling Project (the `PROJECT` contract) that controls marketing wallet — or owner setting a new PROJECT via setProject — can redirect this privilege
Owner can also unilaterally drain via same function
Practical exploit path: a compromised or misconfigured marketing wallet completely sidesteps any owner-only intent and yields arbitrary recipient transfer

triage.drop_reason: Verification not run; this is closer to centralization-risk / privileged action than a code defect. Severity: low/info per most bounty programs (admin keys can rug). Documented for completeness because marketingAddress is sourced via external IProject call — if Project contract is upgradeable / mutable / has weaker access control, the trust boundary is wider than typical owner-only emergency drain. Worth triaging the IProject contract (not in this case dir) before promoting.
